arxiv-2204-07241.title: The Art of Prompting: Event Detection based on Type Specific Prompts
arxiv-2204-07241.creator: Sijia Wang, Mo Yu, Lifu Huang
arxiv-2204-07241.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sijia Wang, Mo Yu, Lifu Huang. We compare various forms of prompts to represent event types and develop a unified framework to incorporate the event type specific prompts for supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot event detection. The experimental results demonstrate that a well-defined and comprehensive event type prompt can significantly improve the performance of event detection, especially when the annotated data is scarce (few-shot event detection) or not available (zero-shot event detection).

arxiv-2207-01204.title: Adversarial Pairwise Reverse Attention for Camera Performance Imbalance in Person Re-Identification: New Dataset and Metrics
arxiv-2207-01204.creator: Eugene P.W. Ang Shan Lin Rahul Ahuja Nemath Ahmed Alex C. Kot
arxiv-2207-01204.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Eugene P.W. Ang Shan Lin Rahul Ahuja Nemath Ahmed Alex C. Kot. Existing evaluation metrics for Person Re-Identification (Person ReID) models focus on system-wide performance. However, our studies reveal weaknesses due to the uneven data distributions among cameras and different camera properties that expose the ReID system to exploitation. In this work, we raise the long-ignored ReID problem of camera performance imbalance and collect a real-world privacy-aware dataset from 38 cameras to assist the study of the imbalance issue.

arxiv-2211-17138.title: The global land water storage data set release 2 (GLWS2.0) derived via assimilating GRACE and GRACE-FO data into a global hydrological model
arxiv-2211-17138.creator: Helena Gerdener, Jürgen Kusche, Kerstin Schulze, Petra Döll, Anna Klos
arxiv-2211-17138.description: Abstract We describe the new global land water storage data set GLWS2.0, which contains total water storage anomalies (TWSA) over the global land except for Greenland and Antarctica with a spatial resolution of 0.5 ∘ , covering the time frame 2003 to 2019 without gaps, and including uncertainty quantification. arxiv-2212-07352.title: Bi-Noising Diffusion: Towards Conditional Diffusion Models with Generative Restoration Priors
arxiv-2212-07352.creator: Kangfu Mei, Nithin Gopalakrishnan Nair, Vishal M. Patel
arxiv-2212-07352.description: Abstract Conditional diffusion probabilistic models can model the distribution of natural images and can generate diverse and realistic samples based on given conditions. However, oftentimes their results can be unrealistic with observable color shifts and textures. We believe that this issue results from the divergence between the probabilistic distribution learned by the model and the distribution of natural images.

arxiv-2303-16087.title: Elimination Techniques for Algorithmic Differentiation Revisited
arxiv-2303-16087.creator: Uwe Naumann, Erik Schneidereit, Simon Märtens, Markus Towara
arxiv-2303-16087.description: Abstract All known elimination techniques for (first-order) algorithmic differentiation (AD) rely on Jacobians to be given for a set of relevant elemental functions. Realistically, elemental tangents and adjoints are given instead. They can be obtained by applying software tools for AD to the parts of a given modular numerical simulation.

arxiv-2303-17615.title: Utilizing Reinforcement Learning for de novo Drug Design
arxiv-2303-17615.creator: Hampus Gummesson Svensson, Christian Tyrchan, Ola Engkvist, Morteza Haghir Chehreghani
arxiv-2303-17615.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hampus Gummesson Svensson, Christian Tyrchan, Ola Engkvist, Morteza Haghir Chehreghani. Deep learning-based approaches for generating novel drug molecules with specific properties have gained a lot of interest in the last few years. Recent studies have demonstrated promising performance for string-based generation of novel molecules utilizing reinforcement learning.

arxiv-2309-11761.title: CASM Monte Carlo: Calculations of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of complex multicomponent crystals
arxiv-2309-11761.creator: Brian Puchala, John C. Thomas, Anton Van der Ven
arxiv-2309-11761.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Brian Puchala, John C. Thomas, Anton Van der Ven. Monte Carlo techniques play a central role in statistical mechanics approaches for connecting macroscopic thermodynamic and kinetic properties to the electronic structure of a material. This paper describes the implementation of Monte Carlo techniques for the study multicomponent crystalline materials within the Clusters Approach to Statistical Mechanics (CASM) software suite, and demonstrates their use in model systems to calculate free energies and kinetic coefficients, study phase transitions, and construct first-principles based phase diagrams.

arxiv-2402-16746.title: Asymptotic-preserving and energy stable dynamical low-rank approximation for thermal radiative transfer equations
arxiv-2402-16746.creator: Chinmay Patwardhan, Martin Frank, Jonas Kusch
arxiv-2402-16746.description: Abstract The thermal radiative transfer equations model temperature evolution through a background medium as a result of radiation. When a large number of particles are absorbed in a short time scale, the dynamics tend to a non-linear diffusion-type equation called the Rosseland approximation.

arxiv-2410-01930.creator: Ghada Sokar, Johan Obando-Ceron, Aaron Courville, Hugo Larochelle, Pablo Samuel Castro
arxiv-2410-01930.description: Abstract The use of deep neural networks in reinforcement learning (RL) often suffers from performance degradation as model size increases. While soft mixtures of experts (SoftMoEs) have recently shown promise in mitigating this issue for online RL, the reasons behind their effectiveness remain largely unknown.

arxiv-2503-09823.description: Abstract . This paper offers a new privacy approach for the growing ecosystem of services—ranging from open banking to healthcare—dependent on sensitive personal data sharing between individuals and third-parties. arxiv-2504-00892.title: Discovery of a new flaring class in GRS 1915+105 using AstroSat
arxiv-2504-00892.creator: Ruchika Dhaka, J.S. Yadav, Ranjeev Misra, Pankaj Jain
arxiv-2504-00892.description: Abstract Highly variable Black Hole X-ray Binary (BHXB) GRS 1915+105 has shown many flaring classes when the source oscillates between the High Soft state (HS) and the Hard Intermediate state (HIMS) with a transition time of less than 10 s. The X-ray flux is anti-correlated with hardness ratio (HR2) during these X-ray flaring classes.

arxiv-2506-12848.title: Towards Fine-Grained Emotion Understanding via Skeleton-Based Micro-Gesture Recognition
arxiv-2506-12848.creator: Hao Xu, Lechao Cheng, Yaxiong Wang, Shengeng Tang, Zhun Zhong
arxiv-2506-12848.description: Abstract We present our solution to the MiGA Challenge at IJCAI 2025, which aims to recognize micro-gestures (MGs) from skeleton sequences for the purpose of hidden emotion understanding. MGs are characterized by their subtlety, short duration, and low motion amplitude, making them particularly challenging to model and classify.

arxiv-2507-09175.title: Combining (post-)Newtonian ideas with quasi-equilibrium (QE) sequence analysis for black hole-neutron star (BHNS) gravitational wave events.
arxiv-2507-09175.creator: Antonio Lanza, Samuel D. Tootle, Andrea Lapi
arxiv-2507-09175.description: Abstract In this paper we present quasi-equilibrium models of black hole-neutron star (BHNS) binaries with mass and spin values compatible with parameter estimates derived from gravitational radiation events GW200105 and GW200115, events consistent with the merger of BHNSs. Using the FUKA initial-data framework, we determine the location of ISCO (Innermost Stable Circular Orbit) and radius of mass-shedding.

arxiv-2512-08909.title: Architecture Design for Rise/Fall Asymmetry Glitch Minimization in Current-Steering DACs
arxiv-2512-08909.creator: Ramin Babaee 1 , Shahab Oveis Gharan 2 , and Martin Bouchard 1
arxiv-2512-08909.description: Abstract Current-steering digital-to-analog converter (DAC)is a prominent architecture that is commonly used in high-speed applications such as optical communications. One of the shortcomings of this architecture is the output glitches that are input dependent and degrade the dynamic performance of the DAC. We investigate DACglitches that arise from asymmetry in the fall/rise response of DAC switches.
